title: Exact ringed pullback on ordinary Hom complexes respects signed source shifts
statement:
Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),S)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),R)$ be a morphism of small ringed topoi with commutative ring sheaves, meaning a geometric inverse image $f^{-1}$ and a ring map $f^{-1}R\to S$. Assume that module pullback $F=f^*=S\otimes_{f^{-1}R}f^{-1}(-)$ is exact. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], ordinary sheaf tensor and Hom [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pur-sheaf-hom], their closed adjunction [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], and the canonical tensor comparison $F(V\otimes_R W)\cong FV\otimes_S FW$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor]. Apply $F$ termwise to integer-indexed cochain complexes. For arbitrary complexes $E,I$ of $R$-modules, let $H(E,I)=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(E,I)$ and $H'$ be the corresponding $S$-module Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex]. For every $n,p\in\mathbf Z$, transpose the map
$$F(H(E,I)^n)\otimes_S FE^p\xrightarrow{\sim}F(H(E,I)^n\otimes_R E^p)\xrightarrow{F(\mathrm{ev}_{n,p})}FI^{p+n},$$
where $\mathrm{ev}_{n,p}$ is evaluation after the $p$th product projection of the Hom complex. These transposes are the product projections of a chain map $c_{E,I}:F H(E,I)\to H'(FE,FI)$, natural contravariantly in chain maps of $E$ and covariantly in chain maps of $I$.

Use the cohomological shifts $E[m]^p=E^{p+m}$ with differential $(-1)^m d_E$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. There are signed chain isomorphisms $s_{E,I,m}:H(E[m],I)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(E,I)[-m]$, with degree-$n$, $p$ component $f\mapsto(-1)^{mn}f^{p-m}$, and likewise $s'$ on $\mathcal D$. With the termwise identification $F(E[m])=(FE)[m]$, for every $m\in\mathbf Z$,
$$s'_{FE,FI,m}\circ c_{E[m],I}=c_{E,I}[-m]\circ F(s_{E,I,m}).$$
Neither $E$ nor $I$ is assumed bounded, flat or injective. No invertibility of $c$, preservation of infinite products by $F$, or derived Hom comparison is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0GMX, remark-pullback-internal-hom; extension to Hom complexes using sites-cohomology.tex, section-hom-complexes (Tag 0A8X) and lemma-RHom-triangulated (Tag 08JC). Agent formulation of the signed chain-level calculation.

proof.text: Write $H^n=H(E,I)^n$ and let $\theta_{V,W}:F(V\otimes_R W)\cong FV\otimes_S FW$ be the natural tensor comparison. The exact module functor $F$ is additive, so it preserves sums, negatives and integer multiples of morphisms. For each $n,p$, set $a_{n,p}=F(\mathrm{ev}_{n,p})\circ\theta_{H^n,E^p}^{-1}$. The tensor-Hom adjunction on $\mathcal D$, using tensor symmetry to put $FE^p$ first, transposes $a_{n,p}$ to $q_{n,p}:FH^n\to\mathcal Hom_S(FE^p,FI^{p+n})$. By the defining product universal property of $H'(FE,FI)^n$, there is a unique $c^n$ with these projections. Transposition is additive: evaluate a sum of transposes and use the bilinearity of evaluation to obtain the sum of their uncurried maps. This construction only uses the product on $\mathcal D$; it makes no assertion about applying $F$ to a product. In Lean reuse the already proved independent-coefficient tensor–Hom equivalence from the K-injective Hom-complex construction. Its inverse, composed with the braiding, defines uncurry with the tensor factors in evaluation order. Prove uncurry naturality from the three naturality identities of that equivalence and the braiding identity. The sectionwise formula for the equivalence and the sheafification adjunction unit give the pure-tensor normalization.

source.place: Tags 03EO (lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor), 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), 0GMX (remark-pullback-internal-hom); agent construction using Tag 0A8X, section-hom-complexes.

proof.text:
Let $\delta^n$ denote the differential of $H(E,I)$. The defining Hom differential, evaluated at its $p$th component, says
$$\mathrm{ev}_{n+1,p}\circ(\delta^n\otimes1)=d_I^{p+n}\circ\mathrm{ev}_{n,p}-(-1)^n\mathrm{ev}_{n,p+1}\circ(1\otimes d_E^p).$$
Apply the additive functor $F$ and precompose with $\theta_{H^n,E^p}^{-1}$. Naturality of $\theta$ changes this into
$$a_{n+1,p}\circ(F\delta^n\otimes1)=F(d_I^{p+n})\circ a_{n,p}-(-1)^n a_{n,p+1}\circ(1\otimes Fd_E^p).$$
Under the natural closed adjunction, the left side is the transpose of the $p$th projection of $c^{n+1}\circ F\delta^n$, and the right side is the transpose of that of $\delta'{}^n\circ c^n$. The adjunction is injective on morphisms, and product projections jointly determine a morphism. Thus these two morphisms agree for every $n$, so $c$ is a chain map.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), displayed differential; agent evaluation calculation using sites-modules Tags 03EO and 03EL.

proof.text:
For chain maps $u:E'\to E$ and $v:I\to I'$, write $h=H(u,v):H(E,I)\to H(E',I')$. By the componentwise definition of $h$, the $p$th evaluation satisfies
$$\mathrm{ev}^{E',I'}_{n,p}\circ(h^n\otimes1)=v^{p+n}\circ\mathrm{ev}^{E,I}_{n,p}\circ(1\otimes u^p).$$
Apply $F$ and use naturality of $\theta$. The resulting equality says that, after projection to $\mathcal Hom_S(FE'^p,FI'^{p+n})$ and transposition, both $c_{E',I'}\circ Fh$ and $H'(Fu,Fv)\circ c_{E,I}$ are the map
$$F(v^{p+n})\circ a^{E,I}_{n,p}\circ(1\otimes Fu^p).$$
Injectivity of the adjunction and the product universal property give the required naturality in both variables.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes); agent componentwise naturality calculation with sites-modules Tags 03EO and 03EL.

proof.text: Use the shifts specified in the statement. A degree-$n$ family in $H(E[m],I)$ has components $f^r:E^{r+m}\to I^{r+n}$. Define $(s^nf)^p=(-1)^{mn}f^{p-m}$, which has source $E^p$ and target $I^{p+n-m}$. Its inverse in degree $n$ sends $g\in H(E,I)^{n-m}$ to the family $f^r=(-1)^{mn}g^{r+m}$. These are maps of sheaves by the product universal property, and the two composites are identities since the reindexings are inverse and $(-1)^{2mn}=1$. The Lean proof reuses ordinaryLeftShift, whose inverse has precisely this signed reindexing. Compose the direct formula with its inverse, cancel the two signs, and transport the source index along (p-m)+m=p to obtain the requested formula.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes); agent signed reindexing with the cohomological shift convention in the statement.

proof.text:
Check that $s$ is a chain map by comparing degree $n$ to degree $n+1$ after each projection $p$. Expansion of $s^{n+1}\delta f$ gives
$$(-1)^{mn+m}d_I^{p+n-m}f^{p-m}-(-1)^{mn+n}f^{p-m+1}d_E^p.$$
Expansion of $d_{H(E,I)[-m]}s^nf$ gives the same expression: its outer differential sign is $(-1)^m$, and its Hom precomposition sign is $-(-1)^{n-m}$. The identities $m(n+1)=mn+m$ and $(-1)^{2m}=1$ give precisely the two displayed coefficients. Hence $s$ is a chain isomorphism. This computation takes place on either ringed site, so it also constructs $s'$. This chain-isomorphism calculation is already proved by ordinaryLeftShift and is reused rather than repeated.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), displayed differential; agent signed calculation underlying Tag 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated).

proof.text:
Since $F((-1)^m d)=(-1)^mF(d)$, termwise pullback identifies $F(E[m])$ with $(FE)[m]$, and likewise identifies $F(H[-m])$ with $(FH)[-m]$. Fix $n,p$ and put $B=H(E[m],I)^n$ and $\sigma=s^n:B\to H(E,I)^{n-m}$. Directly from the formula for $s$,
$$\mathrm{ev}^{E,I}_{n-m,p}\circ(\sigma\otimes1)=(-1)^{mn}\mathrm{ev}^{E[m],I}_{n,p-m}.$$
Project both sides of the asserted comparison square to $\mathcal Hom_S(FE^p,FI^{p+n-m})$ and transpose. For $s'\circ c_{E[m],I}$ the result is
$$(-1)^{mn}F(\mathrm{ev}^{E[m],I}_{n,p-m})\circ\theta_{B,E^p}^{-1}.$$
For $c_{E,I}[-m]\circ F(s)$ the result is
$$F(\mathrm{ev}^{E,I}_{n-m,p})\circ\theta_{H(E,I)^{n-m},E^p}^{-1}\circ(F\sigma\otimes1).$$
Naturality of $\theta$ rewrites the latter as $F(\mathrm{ev}^{E,I}_{n-m,p}\circ(\sigma\otimes1))\circ\theta_{B,E^p}^{-1}$. The displayed evaluation identity and additivity of $F$ make this exactly the former expression. Injectivity of transposition and product projection extensionality prove equality of the chain maps.
